items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess and use up to 1.5 ounces (about 42 g) of cannabis. Residents may also keep up to 5 ounces in a locked container at home or carry it in a locked glovebox or car boot. Cannabis can't be smoked or vaped anywhere tobacco smoking or vaping is banned, and any use is banned in state parks and on state beaches and waters. Towns can ban use in their public areas and set fines.

Hemp products with more than 1 mg of THC per serving or 5 mg per container (or over 0.3% THC for flower) count as cannabis in Connecticut and may be sold only by licensed cannabis retailers and dispensaries; selling them anywhere else is illegal. THC-infused drinks are a separate class, sold only at cannabis retailers and package stores with an endorsement.

Package stores (bottle shops) may sell from 8 am to 10 pm Monday to Saturday and from 10 am to 6 pm on Sunday. There are no package store sales on Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day or New Year's Day. Towns can set shorter hours.

laws.rule: Drivers in Connecticut may not use a hand-held mobile phone or other mobile electronic device while driving (General Statutes 14-296aa). Other distracted driving is a separate offence with the same fines. Hands-free use is allowed for adult drivers.
